docs.title: Harpertoken ConvAI Fine-tuning
docs.text:
This project provides scripts to fine-tune the harpertokenConvAI model (a DistilBERT-based question answering model) on a subset of the SQuAD dataset, optimized for Mac M1 with 8GB RAM using MPS acceleration.

The full API and scripts are organized for easy extension and customization.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Clone or set up the project (assuming local setup): 

    # Project is already in /Users/niladri/Desktop/model
cd /Users/niladri/Desktop/model

  2. Create Virtual Environment: 

    python3 -m venv venv

  3. Activate Virtual Environment: 

    source venv/bin/activate

  4. Install Dependencies: 

    pip install -r requirements.txt
# Optional: Install code quality tools
pip install black flake8 mypy

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: The builder script (run.sh) orchestrates the fine-tuning process with configurable options.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text: ./run.sh

docs.title: Interactive Configuration
docs.text:
When you run ./run.sh, it will prompt you for configuration options interactively:

  • Dataset: Choose the dataset (default: squad)
  • Task: Task type (default: qa)
  • Tune: Enable hyperparameter tuning with Optuna (y/n, default: n)
  • If tuning is disabled:
  • Epochs: Number of training epochs (default: 1)
  • Batch: Batch size (default: 2)
  • LR: Learning rate (default: 2e-5)
  • Upload: Upload to Hugging Face after training (y/n, default: n)

The script will then proceed with training and evaluation based on your inputs.

docs.title: API Serving
docs.text:
After training, serve the model via API: 

pip install fastapi uvicorn
python scripts/api.py  # Or uvicorn scripts.api:app --reload

API Endpoints: - GET /: API info - POST /predict: QA prediction (json: {"question": "...", "context": "..."})

docs.title: Configuration File
docs.text:
Use config.yaml for persistent settings: 

dataset: squad
epochs: 2
batch_size: 4
learning_rate: 0.00005
upload: true

The CLI loads from config.yaml and uses as prompt defaults.

This will: - Load and preprocess the dataset. - Fine-tune the model with specified params. - Evaluate on sample questions. - Optionally upload to harpertoken/harpertokenConvAI-finetuned.

docs.title: Uploading to Hugging Face
docs.text:
Set HF_TOKEN env var for uploads: 

export HF_TOKEN=your_token
./run.sh --upload

Get token from Hugging Face settings.

docs.title: Manual Usage
docs.text:
If you prefer to run scripts individually:

  1. Train the Model: 

    python scripts/train.py
    Loads the model, preprocesses a small SQuAD subset, and fine-tunes for 1 epoch.

  2. Evaluate the Model: 

    python scripts/evaluate.py
    Loads the fine-tuned model from results/ and answers sample questions.

docs.title: Request & Response Types
docs.text: The scripts use standard Hugging Face transformers types. For custom datasets, modify scripts/data_prep.py to return tokenized datasets with required fields (input_ids, attention_mask, start_positions, end_positions).

docs.title: Handling Errors
docs.text:
If training fails due to memory issues, reduce per_device_train_batch_size in scripts/train.py. For MPS errors, ensure PyTorch is installed with MPS support.

Common errors: - CUDA out of memory: Reduce batch size. - ModuleNotFoundError: Ensure venv is activated and dependencies installed.

docs.title: Customizing Training
docs.text: Edit scripts/train.py to adjust: - num_train_epochs: Increase for better performance (monitor RAM). - learning_rate: Tune for convergence. - Dataset: Modify data_prep.py to use custom QA datasets.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Training logs are printed to console. For more verbose logging, set logging_steps lower in TrainingArguments.

docs.title: Accessing Raw Outputs
docs.text: The evaluation script prints answers with confidence scores. To access raw model outputs, modify scripts/evaluate.py to return full predictions.

docs.title: Custom Datasets
docs.text: To use a custom dataset: 1. Update load_and_preprocess_data in scripts/data_prep.py. 2. Ensure the dataset has question, context, and answers columns.

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
• scripts/: Python scripts for data prep, training, and evaluation.
  • data/: Placeholder for custom datasets.
  • models/: Placeholder for saved models.
  • results/: Training outputs and checkpoints.
  • __version__.py: Version information.
  • requirements.txt: Dependencies.
  • pyproject.toml: Project configuration and tool settings.
  • config.yaml: Default configuration for builds.
  • Dockerfile: Docker container configuration.
  • run.sh: Orchestration script.
  • scripts/: Python scripts for fine-tuning.
  • tests/: Unit tests.
  • .github/: GitHub Actions workflows.
  • venv/: Virtual environment.

docs.title: CI/CD
docs.text:
This project uses GitHub Actions for continuous integration and Docker for containerization.

  • Linting: Flake8, Black, MyPy on every push/PR.
  • Testing: Pytest unit tests, syntax checks, and import tests.
  • Docker Build: Builds and pushes image to Docker Hub and GHCR on main branch.

Workflow: .github/workflows/ci.yml

docs.text: Build and run the project in a container.

docs.text:
• Docker Hub: docker pull <username>/harpertoken-convai-finetune
  • GHCR: docker pull ghcr.io/<username>/<repo>/harpertoken-convai-finetune

Dockerfile: Dockerfile

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Run tests locally: 

pip install pytest
pytest tests/

Tests include data preprocessing validation.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python >= 3.14
  • PyTorch with MPS support (Mac M1)
  • 8GB RAM minimum
  • Supported runtimes: macOS with Apple Silicon

docs.title: Git Hooks and Conventional Commits
docs.text: This project uses git hooks for code quality and conventional commit standards.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Enable Pre-commit Hook (code quality): 

    cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit
chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit

  2. Enable Commit Hook (conventional commits): 

    cp scripts/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg
chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg

  3. Rewrite Existing Messages (if needed): 

    ./scripts/rewrite_msg.sh <commit-hash>  # For single commit
./scripts/rewrite_msg.sh <start>..<end>  # For range
git push --force  # After rewriting

docs.title: Commit Message Format
docs.text:
• Start with type: feat:, fix:, docs:, style:, refactor:, test:, chore:, perf:, ci:, build:, revert:
  • Description in lowercase
  • First line ≤40 characters

Example: feat: add conventional commit hook

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
1. Fork the repo.
  2. Create a feature branch.
  3. Make changes and test.
  4. Submit a pull request with conventional commit messages.

For issues, open a GitHub issue.

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text:
Q: How to increase training data? A: Edit select(range(1000)) in data_prep.py to a larger range.

Q: Can this run on other hardware? A: Yes, modify device to 'cuda' for GPU or 'cpu' for CPU-only.

Q: What if I want to deploy the model? A: Use Hugging Face's model upload after training.

docs.title: Semantic Versioning
docs.text:
This project follows SemVer for releases. Backwards-incompatible changes will be in major versions.

We appreciate feedback; open an issue for suggestions.

docs.title: CI/CD
docs.text:
This project uses GitHub Actions for continuous integration, model training, and Docker for containerization.

  • Linting: Flake8, Black, MyPy on every push/PR.
  • Testing: Pytest unit tests, syntax checks, import tests, and post-training validation.
  • Training: Fine-tunes the model on a SQuAD subset with configurable epochs/batch/LR.
  • Hugging Face Upload: Pushes fine-tuned model and tokenizer to HF Hub with model card (requires HF_TOKEN secret).
  • Docker Build: Builds and pushes image to Docker Hub and GHCR on main branch.

Workflows: .github/workflows/ci.yml (CI/training), .github/workflows/docs.yml (MkDocs deployment to GitHub Pages on main branch)
